newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL-CALGARY FLAMES RELEASE COACH PIERRE PAGE.
newsitem.headline: NHL-CALGARY FLAMES RELEASE COACH PIERRE PAGE.

text.p: The Calgary Flames have released Pierre Page as coach, the team announced Wednesday. No one has yet been named to replace him.
Page was let go after he asked to be given a two-year extension on his existing contract or be released, Flames executive vice president Alan Coates said.
"He is therefore released to pursue other coaching opportunities with any team in the National Hockey League," said Coates. "We thank Pierre for his contributions and wish him the best of luck."
"I asked them if they wanted someone who has been around here when they rebuild over the next three years and I wanted to be a part of it," said Page.

"When they hesitated, I had to go my way, and they will do their thing. I wanted to stay and give long-term stability to this organisation. I wanted to be around the next time this organisation winds the Stanley Cup."
Coates added that any team in the Pacific Division must seek written consent before talking to Page, who had one year left on his contract.
The Flames finished in fourth place in the Pacific Division with a 32-41-9 record this past season and did not make the playoffs.

"This just came up in the last 7-10 days," said Coates. "We were expecting to go ahead with Page as coach next year, but when he asked to what amounts to a five-year commitment, we weren't sure we would give that to him or anyone.
"I made the decision and this was hard because Pierre and I go back 17 years."
In two seasons as coach, Page was just 66-78-20. The Flames made the playoffs in the first season under Page but were swept in four games by the Chicago Blackhawks.
Calgary has yet to win a playoff series since winning the Stanley Cup in 1989, losing six opening-round series and failing to make the playoffs on two other occasions.
The Flames were the third NHL coaching job for Page, who also was in charge of the Minnesota North Stars and the Quebec Nordiques.
The Flames became the ninth NHL team to change coaches since the end of the season.
